entry.title: RAP OData V4 unmanaged query pagination
entry.content:
I am implementing a read operation using an Unmanaged Query in the ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model (RAP) for an OData V4 service and pagination.
According to the official SAP Help Documentation page Implementing an Unmanaged Query, the RAP framework handles "default paging" under the following conditions: 

"To avoid high resource consumption when calling an OData service without using $top each OData service, based on the ABAP RESTful Programming Model uses a default paging. This includes... Adding a __next link with a skiptoken to the response if the response represents a partial listing, which is a subset of all available data records." 


However, during runtime testing, when a request is made without a $top parameter, the automated generation of the pagination token does not work as described.
 
Even when configuring the unmanaged query provider class to artificially simulate a partial backend listing—by setting io_response->set_total_number_of_records() to a high integer value (e.g., 1001) while returning a smaller subset array via io_response->set_data() (e.g., 1 row)—the JSON payload returns no __next link or @odata.nextLink tracking property. It only includes the @odata.count attribute.

Questions:
Paging Engine Execution: Why does the unmanaged query engine fail to append a token tracking link when set_total_number_of_records confirms the delivered data payload is a partial listing? 


OData V4 Format Discrepancies: The documentation explicitly references adding a __next link. For a native OData V4 RAP service, the property should structurally be @odata.nextLink. Is this documentation segment incorrect or outdated, or is the framework failing to adapt the token syntax for V4 endpoints? 


Trigger Criteria: What exact internal threshold or API instruction triggers the "default paging" mentioned in the article for unmanaged queries?

entry.title: Cannot access i18n resource bundle in Controller onInit (Model not loaded yet)
entry.content:

For specific architecture and UX requirements in a KPI application I am building, I need to handle certain text strings inside the Controller instead of binding them directly in the XML View.
However, I am facing a timing issue where the i18n model is not yet loaded or available during the early controller lifecycle hooks.
 
What I have tried so far:
1. Accessing it inside onInit
 
onInit: function () {
    // This fails because the model is not ready yet
    this._oBundle = this.getView().getModel("i18n").getResourceBundle();
}

onBeforeRendering: function () {
    this._oBundle = this.getView().getModel("i18n").getResourceBundle();
},

entry.title: EML MODIFY on another sales order from SD_SLS_* BAdI — BEHAVIOR_ILLEGAL_STATEMENT
entry.content:
S/4HANA 2025, developer extensibility (clean core).

I need to update the quantity of a sales document (a contract, doc type ZCON) via EML when another sales order (child order) that references it — by Customer Reference (VBKD-BSTKD) — is saved.

The update logic itself works: in a standalone class (if_oo_adt_classrun), READ + MODIFY ENTITIES OF I_SalesOrderTP (field RequestedQuantity) + COMMIT ENTITIES runs fine and the value persists, no locks.

The problem is doing it from within the child order's save flow. I don't own the sales order BO, so I hook in via BAdI SD_SLS_CHECK_BEFORE_SAVE (enhancement spot ES_SD_SLS_EXTEND). Two attempts:

  • Without COMMIT ENTITIES: the MODIFY ENTITIES is silently ignored — the contract is not updated. The syntax checker also warns that the statement violates the FUNCTIONAL transactional contract.
  • With COMMIT ENTITIES: runtime dump BEHAVIOR_ILLEGAL_STATEMENT, and the child order is not saved.

So updating the contract from inside the check BAdI is clearly not the way. What is the clean-core pattern to trigger a post-commit update of the contract from a sales order save? Options I'm considering: BGPF (Background Processing Framework), a RAP business event via a container BO, or an Application Job.

Which is the recommended approach for this scenario?

Thanks!

entry.title: AUTHORITY-CHECK returns values not maintained in Business Role – SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition
entry.content:
We are working on the FG (Finished Goods) screen in SAP Public Cloud, where we need to control authorization based on different fields and operations.

One of the fields in the FG screen is a Shift dropdown. This dropdown has 3 possible values:

  • DAY – Day Shift
  • NGT – Night Shift
  • GEN – General Shift

The requirement is that the user should only be authorized for the Shift values that are maintained in their Business Role.

For example, suppose a Business Role has the following authorization:

Application: FG
Operation: 0010
Shift: GEN

In this case, when the user accesses the FG screen, the expected authorization should be:

  • GEN → Authorized
  • DAY → Not Authorized
  • NGT → Not Authorized

Technically, we have created a Global Authorization Class for performing the authorization checks, a Field-Level Authorization Class for checking authorization for individual fields, and a Behavior Implementation Class that calls these authorization methods and returns the result to the FG screen.

The issue we are facing is with the actual authorization check.

During debugging, we are checking each Shift value separately. For example:

GEN → AUTHORITY-CHECK → sy-subrc = 0 → Authorized

This is correct because GEN is assigned in the Business Role.

But when we check:

DAY → AUTHORITY-CHECK → sy-subrc = 0 → Authorized

and

NGT → AUTHORITY-CHECK → sy-subrc = 0 → Authorized

These are also returning authorized, even though DAY and NGT were not assigned in the Business Role.

We also tested the standard AUTHORITY-CHECK directly during debugging, without using our authorization wrapper method. Even there, DAY and NGT are returning:

sy-subrc = 0

So it does not appear to be an issue with our wrapper logic or with assigning rv_ok = X.

We are seeing the same type of behavior with some of the other authorization fields as well: values that are not explicitly maintained in the Business Role are still passing the authorization check.

1.Global class -   METHOD can_work_on.

  IF iv_inchg IS NOT INITIAL

     AND iv_machine IS NOT INITIAL

     AND iv_biltyp IS NOT INITIAL.

    AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT 'ZPP_PRDEXE'

      ID 'ZPPAPP'   FIELD iv_app

      ID 'ZPPOPER'  FIELD iv_oper

      ID 'ZPPSHIFT' FIELD iv_shift

      ID 'ZPPINCHG' FIELD iv_inchg

      ID 'ZPPMACH'  FIELD iv_machine

      ID 'ZPPBLTYP' FIELD iv_biltyp.

  ELSE.

 

    AUTHORITY-CHECK OBJECT 'ZPP_PRDEXE'

      ID 'ZPPAPP'   FIELD iv_app

      ID 'ZPPOPER'  FIELD iv_oper

      ID 'ZPPSHIFT' FIELD iv_shift

      ID 'ZPPINCHG' DUMMY

      ID 'ZPPMACH'  DUMMY

      ID 'ZPPBLTYP' DUMMY.

  ENDIF.

  rv_ok = xsdbool( sy-subrc = 0 ).

ENDMETHOD.

 

2.Behaviour Class - DATA(lv_gen_auth) = zcl_pp_auth=>can_work_on(

        iv_app   = zcl_pp_auth=>app-fg_pipes

        iv_oper  = lv_operation

        iv_shift = 'GEN' ).

      DATA(lv_day_auth) = zcl_pp_auth=>can_work_on(

        iv_app   = zcl_pp_auth=>app-fg_pipes

        iv_oper  = lv_operation

        iv_shift = 'DAY' ).

      DATA(lv_ngt_auth) = zcl_pp_auth=>can_work_on(

        iv_app   = zcl_pp_auth=>app-fg_pipes

        iv_oper  = lv_operation

        iv_shift = 'NGT' ).

      ls_result-ShiftGeneralAuth = lv_gen_auth.

      ls_result-ShiftDayAuth     = lv_day_auth.

      ls_result-ShiftNightAuth   = lv_ngt_auth.

entry.title: how to Handle a Assertion_failed Dump in SAP ABAP ?
entry.content:
Hi Experts,

We have a custom ABAP report running in background (SM37) that loops through a set of sales orders and updates them using SD_SALESDOCUMENT_CHANGE alongside custom BAPI extensions (BAPE_VBAP) and pricing conditions.

While standard catchable exceptions (CX_ROOT) are safely handled by our TRY...CATCH blocks, we occasionally encounter hard kernel short dumps such as ASSERTION_FAILED inside standard SAP classes (e.g., CL_SD_SLS_TRANS_MGR=>IF_SD_SLS_TRANS_MGR_INT~SET_TRANSACTION_STATE). Because these assertions trigger an immediate kernel abort, they bypass our TRY...CATCH blocks and crash the entire background job.

My Questions:

Since standard class assertions without checkpoint groups cannot be caught via TRY...CATCH or CX_SY_ASSERT, what is the recommended ABAP design pattern to isolate such failures?

entry.title: Fiori Elements OData V2: Incorrect object-page header and navigation hierarchy in a nested RAP BO
entry.content:
I am developing a custom transactional application using the ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model (RAP) in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. The application uses managed RAP business objects, CDS view entities, projection views, behavior definitions, and a Fiori Elements UI exposed through an OData V2 UI service.

My business object has the following composition hierarchy:

  • Customer — root entity

  • Customer Role — child of Customer

  • Customer Address — child of Customer

  • Company Code — child of Customer

  • Tax — child of Company Code

The entities have technical UUID keys, and the child entities are connected through RAP compositions and parent associations.

Issue

The application displays object pages, but the navigation hierarchy and object-page header are not behaving as expected.

For example, on the Customer Address object page, the header displays a slash-separated value resembling:

8001 /

On the Tax object page, the header displays:

8001 / /

The navigation/header behavior appears inconsistent across the composition hierarchy. I want to understand whether this is caused by the RAP composition and association definitions, CDS annotations, or the way Fiori Elements resolves object-page navigation context.

Questions

  1. How does Fiori Elements determine the slash-separated header and navigation context for nested RAP composition entities?

  2. What could cause the object-page header or navigation hierarchy to display incomplete or unexpected values?

  3. Which RAP composition, parent-association, projection, or UI annotation settings should be checked to ensure navigation works correctly across multiple composition levels?
